titleEn: How does anaesthesia "switch off" your consciousness?
summaryEn:
You count backwards from 10. A few seconds later, everything is gone. When you open your eyes again, an operation lasting hours is over, yet to you it seems that no time has passed at all.
What happened?
Anaesthesia is not simply a deep sleep. It is a controlled state of unconsciousness in which drugs temporarily change the way neural networks in the brain and body communicate with one another.
